headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being lured by fake jobs
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) reveals that men recruited for construction work were forced into the Russian Army.
details: Twenty of 30 Bangladeshis allegedly recruited for construction jobs in Russia have been killed after being forced to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war, according to the Special Response Battalion (SRB).

Seventeen of the victims died in a drone strike on their first day at the front, while three others died later, Additional DIG Asaduzzaman, commander of SRB-10, stated during a news conference in Dhaka.
The investigation began after the father of 21-year-old Rajon Hossain, who returned home wounded, filed a human trafficking case.

Rajon was allegedly charged Tk 825,000 for a construction job. After arriving in Russia on May 7, he and about 30 others were forced into the Russian Army, received 21 days of training, and were sent to the front.

A drone strike fractured Rajon’s pelvis and left him unable to move his legs. He reportedly crawled nearly four kilometres to reach a camp and eventually escaped with embassy assistance, returning to Bangladesh on Aug 23.

Two alleged recruiters, Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher Lentu, have been arrested. Investigators say the network operated through three companies: Jabal-e-Nur, RS International, and TS Group, recruiting from nine districts.
The SRB reports that two returnees are recovering in Bangladesh, two others are in a Moscow hospital, and six remain on the battlefield.

headline: Internal rift in Comilla Jamayet: Car vandalized, cocktails exploded over leadership dispute
summary: Tensions flared at the party's city office in Moglotuli on Wednesday evening as two factions clashed over the new Amir election.
details: Clashes broke out between two factions of Comilla city Jamayet-e-Islami over the election of a new Amir and the formation of a new committee.
